title: Etale descent of the reduced Cartier structure on a closed subset
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $Z\subseteq X$ be a closed subset, and let $D=Z_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X$ be its reduced induced closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. For every etale morphism $v:W\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], the pullback closed subscheme $D\times_XW$ is the reduced induced closed subscheme on $v^{-1}(Z)$. If $\{v_i:W_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ is a jointly surjective etale covering, then $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor if and only if every $D\times_XW_i$ is an effective Cartier divisor. Here an effective Cartier divisor is a closed subscheme whose ideal is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal, def-weil-closed-immersion]; the empty divisor is permitted.

source.place: Tag 083C, lemma-characterize-effective-Cartier-divisor, conditions (1)--(3), specialized to schemes. For reduced pullback: literature/stacks-project/descent.tex, Tag 034E, lemma-reduced-local-smooth (etale implies smooth), followed by uniqueness in Schemes Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme.

proof.text: Let I be the vanishing ideal of Z and i its closed immersion. The reduced-induced-closed-subscheme theorem makes its source reduced. For an etale v:W→X, the projection pullback.snd v i is etale by base change, so its source is reduced by etale reducedness. Mathlib Pullback.range_fst and the image assertion for i identify the image of pullback.fst v i with v⁻¹(Z). Apply the uniqueness clause of the reduced-induced-closed-subscheme theorem on W. It identifies the kernel of this projection with the vanishing ideal of v⁻¹(Z) and gives the required isomorphism over W. This avoids the stronger tensor-ideal assertion of reduced-flat-pullback recognition.

source.place: Tags 01J3, 01JT and 034E: uniqueness of the reduced closed structure, image of a pullback, and reducedness under etale base change.

proof.text: An etale morphism is flat. Apply IsInvertible.comap_of_flat to the vanishing ideal of Z. Its comap is by definition the kernel of pullback.fst v i; rewrite it using the equality proved in step 1. This gives invertibility of the reduced preimage ideal for every covering member.

source.place: Tags 02OO and 02GV: flat pullback of effective Cartier ideals and flatness of etale morphisms.

proof.text: Joint surjectivity and the flat, locally finitely presented nature of the etale arrows give membership of their presieve in the fppf precoverage by Mathlib ofArrows_mem_precoverage_iff. Apply the Mathlib fppf-to-fpqc inclusion. Pullback symmetry identifies the kernel of pullback.snd i (v a) with that of pullback.fst (v a) i, hence by step 1 with the reduced preimage ideal. The assumed invertibility of those ideals is therefore precisely the hypothesis of fpqc_cartier_ideal_reflection. Its last conclusion makes i.ker invertible, and ker_subschemeι identifies this ideal with the original vanishing ideal. Together with step 2 this proves the equivalence. No choice of a covering index is made, so the empty family and empty scheme cases are included; the unit ideal also remains allowed.

source.place: Tags 022C and 083C: fppf covers are fpqc and descent of the effective Cartier condition.

lean.statement: theorem etale_reduced_cartier_descent (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (Z : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X) : (∀ (W : Scheme.{u}) (v : W ⟶ X) [Etale v], ∃ e : pullback v (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal Z).subschemeι ≅ (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (Z.preimage v.continuous)).subscheme, e.hom ≫ (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (Z.preimage v.continuous)).subschemeι = pullback.fst v (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal Z).subschemeι) ∧ (∀ {ι : Type*} (W : ι → Scheme.{u}) (v : ∀ i, W i ⟶ X) [∀ i, Etale (v i)], (⋃ i, Set.range (v i).base = Set.univ) → ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal Z).IsInvertible ↔ ∀ i, (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (Z.preimage (v i).continuous)).IsInvertible))
